reason: Selected curation study and modification audit support failure attribution beyond mere recurrence, with explicit consistency regressions in the reduced-data result.

candidates.title: Distinguish recurring model mistakes from harness defects
candidates.rule: Before turning recurring failures into permanent harness rules, aggregate them across tasks and check whether the proposed change repairs a runtime defect or merely forbids a legitimate action the model mishandles.
candidates.passage: Cross-instance aggregation alone does not automatically reduce MSA
candidates.finding: The authors classify 75.61% of modifications as model-specific accommodation for recurrence without FDCR versus 45.45% with collaborative refinement. Recurrence alone can amplify the wrong restriction. These are author-coded modification audits.
models: Qwen3 harness-evolution study; data curation evolves with Qwen3-8B and evaluates Qwen3-32B
candidates.conditions: Recurring failures are prioritized, then collaborative failure analysis refines modification specifications.
candidates.limitations: Author annotations and model-specific setup limit causal interpretation. The reduced-data experiment has lower pass^3 (45% vs 60% full) despite comparable mean and higher pass@3; cheap search is not equivalent reliability. Full FDCR internals and appendices were not reviewed.
candidates.validation_test: Audit proposed rules for unjustified action bans; compare recurrence-only and attributed repairs on unseen models and tasks, tracking preserved valid actions, mean success, all-trial consistency and total evolution cost.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
